Out of the twelve Titans that had come to shape Amphoreus’ land, seas and skies, the Worldbearer was the greatest of them all. His domineering figure towered over the mountain peaks crafted by his four hands and his crown grazed the firmament that separated the world from the stars beyond the sky, yet equally capable of shedding that divinity to embody the same form as the humans he had given shape from the earth.

Several weeks had passed since he had last walked among them. Not since the end of the annual festival where he descended into Okhema and offered his aid to those in need. Smoke wafted from the city’s many temples at the Worldbearer’s feet as the people’s unease deepened and they burnt ritual offerings to placate what must have been the Titan’s anger, keeping his visage and voice from the priests that relied on the Sky Father for guidance. If he was left unappeased then disaster could befall the city. 

There was no way for even the most devout followers to know that the Throne of Worlds was merely sulking.

The God of Creation, the symbol of heroes and saviours, turned away in a flick of white hair that swept like a long cloud across the open sky. Head petulantly turned away, he pouted towards the distant sea.
